muse.fix: Adopt one encoding in §12.3, in both proposals verbatim: 'verification.fault_rate is required and has type null | RATE. For action and perm_action records it MUST be null and fault_rate_contexts MUST be absent. For an oracle record it MUST be a RATE whenever a fault census is asserted or is required to discharge an executable or scheduled acceptance claim; it MAY be null only when the record asserts no fault census, and null discharges no fault-rate obligation.' In 0jq, change the schema line to 'verification: { oracle: i | null, ... fault_rate: null | { ... } }', change 'For action and perm_action records, fault_rate MUST be absent' to 'MUST be null', and change the fixture migration sentence to 'both action fault-rate placeholders become null'. I would take this null encoding over the absent-key encoding because §12.3's schema is closed and the field is currently required; an explicit null distinguishes 'no census' from a malformed omission.
muse.problem: 0jq and checker-fault-rate, both in this dossier and both proposed as 0.9 K repairs to ISA §12.3, give incompatible MUSTs for the same field. 0jq: schema 'fault_rate?: { ... }', 'fault_rate may be absent when no oracle fault census is asserted', 'For action and perm_action records, fault_rate MUST be absent', and its fixture migration says both action placeholders 'are omitted'. Checker-fault-rate: 'verification.fault_rate: null | RATE', 'For kind=oracle, verification.fault_rate MUST be a RATE; null is reserved for action and perm_action', 'For action and perm_action, verification.fault_rate MUST be null', and its migration 'puts fault_rate:null on both' records of the same published controlled-action-09 fixture (verified in this seat: the fixture currently contains two fault_rate placeholder objects and two oracle:null). An action certificate with the key absent is conformant under 0jq and rejected under checker-fault-rate; one with null is the reverse. An oracle structural-only record with no census is conformant under 0jq and rejected under checker-fault-rate. Two conformant checkers of the same declared version would give different verdicts on the same bytes.

muse.fix: Apply the identical harmonized §12.3 sentences given in 0jq-M1. In checker-fault-rate specifically, replace 'For kind=oracle, verification.fault_rate MUST be a RATE; null is reserved for action and perm_action records.' with: 'For kind=oracle, verification.fault_rate MUST be a RATE whenever a fault census is asserted or is required to discharge an executable or scheduled acceptance claim (including every oracle in the complete invocation tree of a bound schedule, via fault_rate_contexts); it MAY be null only when the record asserts no fault census, and null discharges no fault-rate obligation and satisfies no zero-fault gate.' Keep 'For action and perm_action, verification.fault_rate MUST be null and fault_rate_contexts MUST be absent' unchanged, and add a conformance vector: a standalone structural-only oracle record with fault_rate:null is accepted as a structural packet but rejected for any executable acceptance claim that needs a census.
muse.problem: Same incompatibility as 0jq-M1, seen from this proposal: its unconditional 'For kind=oracle, verification.fault_rate MUST be a RATE' forbids exactly the structural-only oracle packets that 0jq (same dossier, same §12.3, same 0.9 K route) legalises with no census, and its 'MUST be null' for actions forbids 0jq's 'MUST be absent'. Neither diff mentions the other's encoding. Applied together as written, the amended §12.3 cannot be satisfied by any single action-record encoding.
